meta.title: feat: ask data-path questions only where the added lines show the pattern
meta.body:
## Summary

The field run on seven kaipu-record PRs found five data-path patterns Wachiman misses (destructive step without re-verification, read error treated as empty, overlapping calls, unbounded wait, stale write-back). Five agents each wrote one question module; this PR merges them and wires them in.

- `src/questions/index.ts`: the registry `QUESTIONS` and `selectQuestions(files)`. It runs every `applies` over each file's added lines, in registry order, once per question.
- `buildBatchPrompt` adds a section "Risks this part's added lines show" right after `FLOW_QUESTIONS` only when a question applies. The answers go in `contracts` and a defect found is also a finding. When none applies, the prompt is byte-identical to today's (tested).
- The engine logs `Data-path questions for part N of M: <ids|none>` per batch, so cost can be attributed later.
- `read-error-as-empty` now skips test files (see below). Imports normalised to the repo's extensionless style.
- ADR 0016 (proposed). I used 0016 because 0014 and 0015 are on the open design PR #80.
- `scripts/questions-firing.ts` is the measurement below. It lives outside `src/` and `bun test`.

Added lines come from the existing `addedLinesOf` (all `+` rows), not a second implementation: GitHub's `patch` has no `+++` header, and excluding `+++` would drop a real added line such as `++i;`.

## Firing table

Measured with `bun scripts/questions-firing.ts niway-dev/kaipu-record 439 449 476 478 479 482 483 484 -- 472 473 475 477 481`. It drops `DEFAULT_EXCLUDE` files, batches with `planBatches` at the default limits, and builds the real prompt with and without the selection. Cells are the number of files where the question fires.

**Data set (the field-run PRs)**

| PR | files | files with any | destructive | read-error | overlapping | bounded-wait | stale-write | batches paying | words added (total / largest batch) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #439 | 17 | 1 (6 %) | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 of 1 | 192 / 192 |
| #449 | 92 | 9 (10 %) | 1 | 0 | 8 | 3 | 2 | 3 of 7 | 1194 / 565 |
| #476 | 14 | 0 (0 %) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 of 2 | 0 / 0 |
| #478 | 41 | 3 (7 %) | 2 | 0 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 1 of 5 | 565 / 565 |
| #479 | 65 | 2 (3 %) | 2 | 1 | 2 | 0 | 1 | 2 of 6 | 883 / 563 |
| #482 | 47 | 3 (6 %) | 2 | 0 | 2 | 1 | 3 | 3 of 6 | 1201 / 565 |
| #483 | 104 | 17 (16 %) | 3 | 1 | 8 | 11 | 1 | 2 of 7 | 1131 / 687 |
| #484 | 3 | 0 (0 %) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 of 1 | 0 / 0 |
| **All** | **383** | **35 (9 %)** | | | | | | **12 of 35** | |

**Contrast set (UI, docs, CI)**

| PR | files | files with any | destructive | read-error | overlapping | bounded-wait | stale-write | batches paying | words added |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #472 docs | 4 | 1 (25 %) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 1 of 1 | 198 / 198 |
| #473 docs | 12 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 of 1 | 0 |
| #475 camera UI | 42 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 of 1 | 0 |
| #477 CI | 2 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 of 1 | 0 |
| #481 CI | 2 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 of 1 | 0 |
| **All** | **62** | **1 (2 %)** | | | | | | **1 of 5** | |

- Data PRs: 9 % of files fire something, and the firing files are the main-process code that stores, moves, deletes or waits (`registry.ts`, `identity.ts`, `move-item.ts`, `settings-overrides.ts`, `sync-state.ts` and similar). Contrast PRs: 2 % of files, one file.
- The one contrast firing is `bounded-wait` on `scripts/check-adr-numbers.ts` (#472): the added lines run a `git fetch` with `timeout: 10_000`. That is a real wait with a constant, so I left it.
- No question fires on most files of the contrast set (max 1 file of 62), so none needed tightening for that reason.

## One trigger I tightened

`read-error-as-empty` fired on **test files**: in the first run, 2 of its 4 firings were `library-vault.sidecar-read.test.ts` (#439) and `move-item.test.ts` (#479). Tests read and write fixtures on purpose, and the question is about production data. It now returns false for test paths (`.test.`, `.spec.`, `__tests__/`, `tests/`, `e2e/`, `fixtures/`), with a test. The table above is after the change. Its firings went from 4 files to 2.

## Cost impact estimate

- **Prompt size (measured):** a batch that fires gets 192 to 687 words, 430 on average (12 batches). Over all 35 batches of the seven data PRs, the sections add 28,353 characters to 2,018,755 (1.4 %). The diffs dominate the prompt, so the section is small next to it.
- **Batches that pay:** 12 of 35 on the data PRs; 1 of 5 on the contrast PRs. Batches with no pattern pay nothing.
- **Not measured:** the larger cost is the extra reading and `contracts` entries the model produces to answer. The field run showed the flow questions raised re-review cost from $0.27 to $0.57 on average. These questions fire on a minority of batches, but I cannot give a dollar figure without a replay.

## What is not measured yet

- **No replay.** Whether these questions find the bugs they were written from (#479 High, #482 unreadable file, `copyToAll`, interleaving, probe, #483 deadline, #478 write-back) when asked of a real model is untested. The firing table shows only where the questions are asked.
- Known trigger misses (details in ADR 0016): `read-error-as-empty` needs the write in the same added lines; `stale-write-back` misses 07a47af's `upgradeDefaultColor`; `bounded-wait` ignores `.tsx`/`.jsx`; `applies` never sees unchanged lines.
- Whether the triggers fire on the *right* files of the data PRs was not checked file by file against the bug locations, only counted.
- The contrast set is five PRs from one repository.

## How to test it yourself

```sh
bun test                                  # 510 pass, 7 skip, 0 fail
bun test src/questions                    # the five modules and the registry
bun scripts/questions-firing.ts niway-dev/kaipu-record 439 449 476 478 479 482 483 484 -- 472 473 475 477 481
```

The script needs `gh` logged in with read access to `niway-dev/kaipu-record`. To see the selection in a run, look for `Data-path questions for part …` in the engine log.

@@ -0,0 +1,106 @@
+# ADR 0016: Data-path questions are chosen by the engine from the added lines
+
+- **Status:** accepted 2026-11-03. Implemented by the pull request that adds this file
+  (`src/questions/`, `buildBatchPrompt`).
+- **Date:** 2026-11-02
+- **Evidence:**
+  - [Field run 2026-11-02](https://github.com/niway-dev/wachiman-benchmarks/blob/main/2026-11-02-field/README.md),
+    section "What to improve in Wachiman", items 1 to 5: the bugs these questions target.
+  - [Batch-level A/B 2026-11-03](https://github.com/niway-dev/wachiman-benchmarks/blob/main/2026-11-03-data-path-questions-ab/README.md):
+    on the five batches that held the 10 missed bugs, two runs per arm, Opus 5.5, the questions
+    took the bugs found at least once from 2 to 7 of 10. Invalid findings stayed at 0, and the cost
+    per batch fell from $0.59 to $0.52, with fewer turns. **The questions were written from the same
+    10 bugs**, so this shows they reach their targets, not that they generalise. Held-out bugs
+    decide that (see the reopen condition).
+- **Numbering:** 0014 and 0015 are taken by the open design pull request #80, so this record is
+  0016.
+
+## Context
+
+On seven kaipu-record pull requests that shipped one feature (about 24,000 added lines), Wachiman
+found 2 of the 11 real Medium-or-higher bugs on the three pull requests all three bots reviewed;
+CodeRabbit found 6 and Pullfrog 4. Auditors traced each miss to the batch that covered the code.
+Five patterns recur:
+
+1. A destructive step (`unlink`, `rm`, "clear every other") that does not re-verify its target, or
+   whose failure still drops the record that would allow a retry.
+2. A read error treated as "empty" and then written back.
+3. Two calls in flight at once on the same cache, map or file.
+4. A probe, poll or loop whose individual calls are bounded and whose total is not.
+5. Cached or deferred state written back over another writer's change.
+
+In each case the batch's summary described the code and approved it. The model had not been asked
+the question: the flow questions (`FLOW_QUESTIONS`, [ADR 0009](0009-investigation-is-requested-by-the-model-and-admitted-by-the-engine.md))
+ask what a new action does, not what a delete is aimed at or what bounds a wait.
+
+## Decision
+
+1. **Five questions, one module each** in `src/questions/`, with the contract `DataPathQuestion`
+   (`id`, `title`, `text` of at most 120 words, `applies(addedLines, filename)`).
+2. **The engine selects them per batch, deterministically.** `selectQuestions(files)` runs every
+   `applies` over the added lines of each file of the batch (rows of the patch that start with `+`,
+   without it) and returns the questions that apply to at least one file, once each, in registry
+   order. No model, no network, no repository read.
+3. **A batch where none applies is unchanged.** Its prompt is byte-identical to the one before
+   this record. Otherwise the prompt gets a section "Risks this part's added lines show" right
+   after `FLOW_QUESTIONS`, with the title and text of each selected question. The answers belong
+   in `contracts`, like the flow questions', and a defect found is reported as a finding as well.
+4. **The selection is logged per batch** (`Data-path questions for part 1 of 3: bounded-wait`), so
+   cost and findings can later be attributed to a question.
+
+## Alternatives rejected
+
+- **Ask all five in every batch.** Every batch would pay the words and, more important, the
+  reading and `contracts` entries the questions provoke, including batches of CSS, docs and CI.
+  v1.4.0's flow questions already raised re-review cost from $0.27 to $0.57 on average
+  (field run), and those apply everywhere. A batch with no delete, no persisted write and no wait
+  gains nothing from these questions.
+- **Let the model decide which to ask.** The failure being fixed is that the model did not think of
+  the question. Asking it to choose among questions repeats that dependence, and ADR 0009 already
+  decided that the engine gathers and admits work while the model judges. Here the engine only
+  decides what to ask, from text; the model still answers and judges.
+- **Score the pull request and gate on the score.** ADR 0009 rejected thresholds from indicators
+  until they are measured; a pattern match on added lines is a smaller claim than a score.
+
+## Consequences
+
+- A batch that shows a pattern pays for the section (up to 120 words per question; on the
+  kaipu-record data pull requests, 12 of 35 batches fired, with 430 words on average, 192 to 687,
+  which is 1.4 % of all the prompt characters those pull requests send) and for whatever extra
+  reading the model does to answer. The second cost is not measured.
+- A trigger is a regex over added lines, so it has known misses and known false alarms. Each module
+  documents its own. The misses that matter:
+  - `read-error-as-empty` needs the write in the same added lines. A `catch` added to a store whose
+    write is unchanged context is missed; a write-less config loader that falls back to defaults is
+    deliberately not asked. It also skips test files.
+  - `stale-write-back` misses the upgrade that produced #478's first bug (`upgradeDefaultColor`,
+    commit `07a47af`): the write and the remembered value are not within its window of added lines.
+  - `bounded-wait` ignores `.tsx` and `.jsx` and UI timing words, so a wait in a component is not
+    asked about; `setTimeout` alone is not a signal.
+  - `overlapping-calls` does not check the order of the await and the write, and `destructive-step`
+    sees only calls it has a name for and a clear call within three added lines of a loop header.
+  - `applies` receives one file's added lines, never the unchanged ones, so a pattern that spans
+    unchanged code is invisible to every trigger.
+- A new question is a new module and a new entry in `QUESTIONS`; nothing else changes.
+- Each question is a hypothesis about what the model misses. Without a replay, a question that
+  never finds a bug still costs on every batch that fires it.
+
+## Non-goals
+
+- Verifying an answer. The engine checks that cited lines exist (`src/contracts.ts`), as for the
+  flow questions, not that the answer is true.
+- Questions for patterns the field run did not show (CSS cascade, risk ordering), and the engine
+  bug about merges from the base branch (items 6 to 8 of the same section).
+- Reading unchanged code in the triggers, or calling the model to classify a file.
+- Changing batching, budgets or the number of calls.
+
+## Reopen if
+
+- A replay of the field-run pull requests (#478, #479, #482, #483) with these questions on finds no
+  more of their real Medium+ bugs than the same engine without them. Then remove the questions that
+  found none.
+- Or the batches that fire cost more than the field run's per-batch average by a margin the owner
+  sets before the replay (proposed: 25 %) without a confirmed finding to show for it.
+- Or the firing rate on a repository's pull requests of the kind the contrast set represents
+  (UI, docs, CI) climbs well above the 2 % of files measured here (proposed: above 20 %). Then
+  tighten the trigger that fires.

+import { describe, expect, test } from "bun:test";
+import { QUESTION } from "./bounded-wait";
+
+const wordCount = (text: string) => text.trim().split(/\s+/).length;
+
+// kaipu-record #482, commit 833ca60 (first head), apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/workspace-settings.ts.
+// Verbatim added lines of the read timeout and `refresh`; `isAvailable` is awaited outside the race (D1/F8).
+const KAIPU_482_ADDED: string[] = [
+  "/** How long a capture waits for a folder file before it counts as unreadable (an evicted file). */",
+  "const READ_TIMEOUT_MS = 2000;",
+  "",
+  "  private async read(path: string): Promise<FolderRead> {",
+  "    const timeout = this.deps.readTimeoutMs ?? READ_TIMEOUT_MS;",
+  "    let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;",
+  "    try {",
+  "      return await Promise.race([",
+  "        readFolderOverrides(path),",
+  "        new Promise<FolderRead>((resolve) => {",
+  '          timer = setTimeout(() => resolve({ kind: "unreadable" }), timeout);',
+  "        }),",
+  "      ]);",
+  "    } catch {",
+  '      return { kind: "unreadable" };',
+  "    } finally {",
+  "      clearTimeout(timer);",
+  "    }",
+  "  }",
+  "",
+  "  /**",
+  "   * Read a workspace's folder file into the cache. A workspace that is not connected has no",
+  "   * readable file. When the active workspace's overrides change because of it (a sync wrote",
+  "   * the file), everyone is told.",
+  "   */",
+  "  async refresh(id: string): Promise<void> {",
+  "    const ws = this.known(id);",
+  "    if (!ws) return;",
+  "    const before = JSON.stringify(this.overridesOf(id));",
+  "    this.reads.set(",
+  "      id,",
+  '      (await this.deps.isAvailable(id)) ? await this.read(ws.path) : { kind: "unreadable" },',
+  "    );",
+  "    if (id === this.deps.activeId() && before !== JSON.stringify(this.overridesOf(id))) {",
+  "      this.deps.changed();",
+  "    }",
+  "  }",
+];
+
+// kaipu-record #483, commit 443a9b0 (first head), apps/kaipu-record/src/main/library/dataless.ts.
+// Verbatim added lines: per-batch stat timeout, sequential batches, unbounded lstat fallback (D11).
+const KAIPU_483_ADDED: string[] = [
+  "/** How long one `stat` batch may take. Answered in milliseconds in the spike; never hangs here. */",
+  "export const STAT_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000;",
+  "function runStatCli(paths: string[]): Promise<{ stdout: string; failed: boolean }> {",
+  "  return new Promise((resolve) => {",
+  "    execFile(",
+  '      "/usr/bin/stat",',
+  '      ["-f", "%f %N", "--", ...paths],',
+  "      { timeout: STAT_TIMEOUT_MS, maxBuffer: 4 * 1024 * 1024 },",
+  '      (error, stdout) => resolve({ stdout: String(stdout ?? ""), failed: error !== null }),',
+  "    );",
+  "  });",
+  "}",
+  "",
+  "/** Which of `paths` are evicted. A missing path is not. Never reads a file's data; never throws. */",
+  "export async function datalessPaths(",
+  "  paths: readonly string[],",
+  "  deps: DatalessDeps = defaultDatalessDeps,",
+  "): Promise<Set<string>> {",
+  "  const evicted = new Set<string>();",
+  "  for (let start = 0; start < paths.length; start += BATCH) {",
+  "    const batch = paths.slice(start, start + BATCH);",
+  '    const { stdout } = await deps.runStat(batch).catch(() => ({ stdout: "", failed: true }));',
+  "    const flags = parseStatFlags(stdout);",
+  "    if (flags.size > 0) {",
+  "      // stat answered: its flags are the truth, and a path it did not print is missing.",
+  "      for (const [path, value] of flags) {",
+  "        if ((value & SF_DATALESS) !== 0) evicted.add(path);",
+  "      }",
+  "      continue;",
+  "    }",
+  "    // stat gave nothing at all (not there, killed by the timeout): the block count is a guess.",
+  "    for (const path of batch) {",
+  "      const info = await deps.lstat(path).catch(() => null);",
+  "      if (info && info.blocks === 0 && info.size > 0) evicted.add(path);",
+  "    }",
+  "  }",
+  "  return evicted;",
+  "}",
+  "",
+];
+
+// kaipu-record #449, commit 1eb0638 (head), apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/index.ts.
+// Verbatim added lines: the 120 s prepare wait that a closing window never answers (F5; Wachiman found it).
+const KAIPU_449_ADDED: string[] = [
+  "const PREPARE_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000;",
+  "",
+  "/**",
+  " * Ask every window to prepare (flush, ask about unsaved work, close editors) and wait for",
+  " * all of them. A window that does not answer in time cancels the switch.",
+  " */",
+  "function prepareWindows(): Promise<boolean> {",
+  "  const windows = BrowserWindow.getAllWindows().filter(",
+  "    (w) => !w.isDestroyed() && !w.webContents.isCrashed(),",
+  "  );",
+  "  return Promise.all(",
+  "    windows.map(",
+  "      (window) =>",
+  "        new Promise<boolean>((resolve) => {",
+  "          const requestId = ++nextRequestId;",
+  "          const timer = setTimeout(() => {",
+  "            pendingPrepares.delete(requestId);",
+  "            resolve(false);",
+  "          }, PREPARE_TIMEOUT_MS);",
+  "          pendingPrepares.set(requestId, (ok) => {",
+  "            clearTimeout(timer);",
+  "            pendingPrepares.delete(requestId);",
+  "            resolve(ok);",
+  "          });",
+  "          window.webContents.send(IPC_CHANNELS.workspacesPrepare, { requestId });",
+  "        }),",
+  "    ),",
+];
+
+describe("bounded-wait question", () => {
+  test("has the contract shape and stays within 120 words", () => {
+    expect(QUESTION.id).toBe("bounded-wait");
+    expect(QUESTION.title.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
+    expect(QUESTION.title).not.toContain("\n");
+    expect(wordCount(QUESTION.text)).toBeLessThanOrEqual(120);
+    expect(QUESTION.text).not.toMatch(/^#/m);
+  });
+
+  describe("applies to the real kaipu-record patterns", () => {
+    test("#482: availability awaited outside the 2 s read race", () => {
+      expect(
+        QUESTION.applies(
+          KAIPU_482_ADDED,
+          "apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/workspace-settings.ts",
+        ),
+      ).toBe(true);
+    });
+    test("#483: per-batch stat timeout over sequential batches with an lstat fallback", () => {
+      expect(
+        QUESTION.applies(KAIPU_483_ADDED, "apps/kaipu-record/src/main/library/dataless.ts"),
+      ).toBe(true);
+    });
+    test("#449: the 120 s prepare wait", () => {
+      expect(
+        QUESTION.applies(KAIPU_449_ADDED, "apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/index.ts"),
+      ).toBe(true);
+    });
+  });
+
+  describe("applies to other timeout, deadline, race, probe, poll and retry code", () => {
+    const cases: [string, string[]][] = [
+      [
+        "AbortSignal.timeout",
+        ["const res = await fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000) });"],
+      ],
+      [
+        "deadline variable",
+        ["const deadline = Date.now() + 10_000;", "if (Date.now() >= deadline) break;"],
+      ],
+      ["timeout option", ["execFile(bin, args, { timeout: 5_000 }, cb);"]],
+      ["Promise.race", ["await Promise.race([work(), gaveUp]);"]],
+      ["poll loop", ["while (!(await isReady())) await poll();"]],
+      [
+        "retry with backoff",
+        ["for (let n = 0; n < retries; n++) {", "  await sleep(backoff * 2 ** n);"],
+      ],
+      ["probe", ["const evicted = await probeDataless(paths);"]],
+    ];
+    for (const [name, lines] of cases) {
+      test(name, () => expect(QUESTION.applies(lines, "src/main/sync.ts")).toBe(true));
+    }
+  });
+
+  describe("never applies to the near misses", () => {
+    test("a UI debounce setTimeout", () => {
+      const lines = [
+        "const timer = setTimeout(() => setQuery(value), 300);",
+        "return () => clearTimeout(timer);",
+      ];
+      expect(QUESTION.applies(lines, "src/lib/use-debounce.ts")).toBe(false);
+      expect(QUESTION.applies(lines, "src/components/search.tsx")).toBe(false);
+    });
+    test("a debounce handle named like a timeout", () => {
+      const lines = [
+        "const timeoutId = setTimeout(() => flush(), DEBOUNCE_MS);",
+        "if (timeoutRef.current) clearTimeout(timeoutRef.current);",
+        "const debounceTimeout = setTimeout(save, 250);",
+      ];
+      expect(QUESTION.applies(lines, "src/lib/save.ts")).toBe(false);
+    });
+    test("a bare setTimeout and a sleep helper in source", () => {
+      const lines = [
+        "const sleep = (ms: number) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));",
+        "setTimeout(() => el.focus(), 0);",
+      ];
+      expect(QUESTION.applies(lines, "src/lib/sleep.ts")).toBe(false);
+    });
+    test("a CSS transition", () => {
+      const css = ["  transition: opacity 200ms ease-in;", "  animation-timeout: 2s;"];
+      expect(QUESTION.applies(css, "src/styles/app.css")).toBe(false);
+      const inJs = ['el.style.transition = "opacity 200ms";', "const hoverTimeout = 200;"];
+      expect(QUESTION.applies(inJs, "src/lib/fade.ts")).toBe(false);
+    });
+    test("an await sleep in a test", () => {
+      const lines = [
+        "await sleep(50);",
+        "const result = await Promise.race([run(), timeout(100)]);",
+      ];
+      for (const file of [
+        "src/sync.test.ts",
+        "src/sync.spec.js",
+        "src/__tests__/sync.ts",
+        "test/sync.ts",
+        "e2e/flow.ts",
+        "src/sync_test.go",
+        "tests/test_sync.py",
+        "src/__mocks__/clock.ts",
+        "src/Button.stories.ts",
+      ]) {
+        expect(QUESTION.applies(lines, file)).toBe(false);
+      }
+    });
+    test("documentation lines", () => {
+      const lines = [
+        "The probe has a 2 s timeout and a deadline of 10 s; retry with backoff.",
+        "Poll every second until Promise.race settles.",
+      ];
+      for (const file of [
+        "docs/adr/0034-probe.md",
+        "README.mdx",
+        "docs/spec.txt",
+        "config.yaml",
+        "package.json",
+      ]) {
+        expect(QUESTION.applies(lines, file)).toBe(false);
+      }
+    });
+    test("comment-only lines in source", () => {
+      const lines = [

+/**
+ * "A wait with no overall bound": a probe, poll, retry, per-item check or loop of awaits whose
+ * individual calls are bounded but whose total is not. The evidence is three kaipu-record pull
+ * requests (a capture-start probe outside its 2 s race, a Library listing whose per-batch 5 s
+ * timeout multiplies across batches, and a deadline checked only between batches). The pattern
+ * the model tends to miss is accepting a constant that looks like a bound without asking what it
+ * bounds, so the question tells it what to compare. FLOW_QUESTIONS item 6 already asks "times out
+ * or never delivers"; this adds the "what bounds the whole operation" check.
+ *
+ * Trigger (all pure regex over lines; no I/O):
+ * - the file is non-test source code: a code extension, not a test, mock, fixture or story path,
+ *   and not .tsx/.jsx (components are where debounces, animations and toasts live);
+ * - at least one added line, ignoring comment-only lines and lines about UI timing
+ *   (debounce, throttle, animation, transition, toast, tooltip, hover), has a wait-bound signal:
+ *   `Promise.race`, `AbortSignal.timeout`, an identifier or option with "timeout" or "deadline"
+ *   in it (`READ_TIMEOUT_MS`, `{ timeout: ... }`, `deadlineMs`), or a probe/poll/retry/backoff.
+ *
+ * Before matching, `setTimeout`, `clearTimeout`, `setInterval`, `clearInterval` and handle names
+ * such as `timeoutId` are blanked, so a bare `setTimeout(fn, 300)` is not a signal on its own:
+ * the delay has to be named by a timeout or deadline to count. A bound-looking constant is the
+ * signal, because that is exactly what the question tells the model to distrust.
+ */

+  /(?:[._-](?:test|spec|e2e)\.[^/]+$|_test\.(?:go|py)$|(?:^|\/)test_[^/]*\.py$|(?:^|\/)(?:__tests__|__mocks__|tests?|e2e|fixtures?|mocks?|stories)\/|\.stories\.)/i;
+
+const COMMENT_ONLY = /^\s*(?:\/\/|\/\*|\*|#)/;
+const UI_TIMING = /debounce|throttle|animat|transition|requestAnimationFrame|toast|tooltip|hover/i;
+
+/** Timer calls and their handles say nothing about a bound; the delay's name does. */
+const TIMER_NOISE = /\b(?:set|clear)(?:Timeout|Interval)\b|\b\w*timeout(?:Id|Ref|Handle)\b/gi;
+
+const WAIT_BOUND_SIGNAL = new RegExp(
+  [
+    String.raw`\bPromise\.race\b`,
+    String.raw`\bAbortSignal\.timeout\b`,
+    String.raw`\b\w*(?:timeout|deadline)\w*\b`,
+    String.raw`probe`,
+    String.raw`\bpoll(?:s|ed|ing|er)?(?![a-z])`,
+    String.raw`\bretr(?:y|ies|ying)`,
+    String.raw`\bbackoff`,
+  ].join("|"),
+  "i",

+  id: "bounded-wait",
+  title: "What bounds the whole wait",
+  text:
+    "For each probe, poll, retry, race or loop of awaits in the added code, name what bounds the " +
+    "whole operation, not one call. A per-call timeout multiplies by the number of sequential " +
+    "calls or batches; a deadline checked only between batches overshoots by one full call. " +
+    "Read what sits outside the timeout or race: an await before the raced call, or a fallback " +
+    "after a timed-out probe (an lstat, a retry), and whether it has its own limit. If a user " +
+    "action waits on it (a hotkey, capture start, a listing), say what they see in the worst " +
+    "case. A constant, or a comment saying it never hangs, is not the bound until you check " +
+    "what it covers.",

+      if (COMMENT_ONLY.test(line) || UI_TIMING.test(line)) return false;
+      return WAIT_BOUND_SIGNAL.test(line.replace(TIMER_NOISE, " "));
+    });
+  },
+};

+ * has no store-like write; a pure async helper only assigns local variables; CSS, markdown and
+ * JSON files are rejected by the extension. The order of the await and the write is not checked,
+ * because both "read, await, write back" and "write, await, roll back" are exposed.
+ */
+const CODE_FILE = /\.(?:[cm]?[jt]s|[jt]sx|py)$/i;
+const SKIPPED_FILE = /(?:\.d\.ts$|\.(?:test|spec|stories)\.[a-z]+$|(?:^|\/)(?:__tests__|__mocks__|tests?)\/)/i;
+const COMMENT_LINE = /^\s*(?:\/\/|\/\*|\*|#)/;
+const AWAIT = /\bawait\b/;
+
+const STORE_WORD = "(?:cache|store|registry|gate|map|queue|pending|inflight|memo|reads|sessions|tokens)";
+const SHARED_WRITES: RegExp[] = [
+  // this.reads.set(...), this.items.push(...), this.machine.update(...)
+  /\bthis\.[\w$]+(?:\.[\w$]+)*\.(?:set|delete|clear|add|push|unshift|splice|pop|shift|update|commit|rebind)\(/,
+  // this.key.activeId = id, this.cache[id] = x, this.total += n
+  /\bthis\.[\w$]+(?:\.[\w$]+|\[[^\]\n]+\])+\s*(?:[-+*|&?]{0,2}=)(?![=>])/,
+  // this.cache = {}, this.last = compute(); not this.deps = deps, not this.x = new Map()
+  /\bthis\.[\w$]+\s*(?:[-+*|&?]{0,2}=)(?![=>])\s*(?!new\b)(?![\w$]+\s*;?\s*$)\S/,
+  // cache.set(...), workspaceGate().rebind(...), store.delete(...)
+  new RegExp(
+    `\\b[\\w$]*${STORE_WORD}[\\w$]*(?:\\(\\))?\\s*\\.(?:set|delete|clear|add|push|splice|update|commit|rebind|remove|reset)\\(`,
+    "i",
+  ),
+  // pendingByKey[key] = ..., cache[id] = ...
+  new RegExp(`\\b[\\w$]*${STORE_WORD}[\\w$]*\\[[^\\]\\n]+\\]\\s*(?:[-+*|&?]{0,2}=)(?![=>])`, "i"),
+  // files and persistent writes
+  /\b(?:writeFile|writeFileSync|appendFile|appendFileSync|rename|renameSync|unlink|unlinkSync|copyFile|truncate|outputFile|writeJson|persist\w*|write_text|write_bytes)\s*\(/,
+  /\bBun\.write\s*\(/,
+  /\bwrite[A-Z][\w$]*\s*\(/,
+];
+
+export const QUESTION: DataPathQuestion = {
+  id: "overlapping-calls",
+  title: "Two calls in flight at once",
+  text: `For each async function here that reads shared state (a cache, map, file or store), awaits, and
+then writes it back, run two calls for the same key that overlap: A starts, B starts, then the awaits
+resume. Does B's write drop A's change, does an older read land after a newer write, or does a record
+end up out of order (a file left "pending")? Is there a per-key lock, queue or serialized tail, and
+do all writers and refreshers of that state go through it, or only this one? A check made before an
+await: is it still true after it? Answer from the code and cite the lines.`,
+  applies(addedLines, filename) {
+    if (!CODE_FILE.test(filename) || SKIPPED_FILE.test(filename)) return false;
+    const code = addedLines.filter((line) => !COMMENT_LINE.test(line));
+    if (!code.some((line) => AWAIT.test(line))) return false;
+    return code.some((line) => SHARED_WRITES.some((write) => write.test(line)));
+  },
+};
